newsitem.title: USA: Mesa to pay $270 mln for WMC's Greenhill.
newsitem.headline: Mesa to pay $270 mln for WMC's Greenhill.

text.p: Mesa Inc said Monday it has agreed to acquire Greenhill Petroleum Corp from WMC Ltd for $270 million.

Greenhill's assets are concentrated in four producing areas and include 522 producing wells; over 200 development projects; significant exploration potential, including a number of subsalt drilling prospects; and 3-D seismic data on some 52,800 gross acres, 49,000 acres net, Mesa said.
The company said the acquisition is accretive for 1997's per share cash flow and positions Mesa to expand cash flow in the future through internally generated projects.
"Based on our development plans, we expect cash flow from the GPC properties of more than $65 million in 1998," it said.

"Mesa has already identified 45 development wells and 132 completions. We intend to initiate 22 of these projects in 1997 and at least 25 in 1998, and plan to invest at least $65 million over the next two years."

With the additional development projects, the company continued, it expects to increase production from the Greenhill properties to over 12,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day from the current 9,300 barrels daily.
"In addition, we have identified a number of exploration opportunities, including a deeper zone and two subsalt prospects, which we expect to evaluate further."
It said Greenhill's January 1 proven reserves totaled 30 million barrels of oil equivalent.

Of the $270 million purchase price, Mesa said, it allocated $180 million to proved reserves and the balance to probable and possible reserves, proprietary seismic data and Greenhill's net assets and working capital.

Giving effect to the Greenhill transaction and the acquisition of 11 million barrels of NGL reserves announced last week, Mesa said, it expects to increase production to 162 billion cubic feet equivalent this year from 128 billion in 1996. Based on current price levels and developemtn plants, Mesa expects cash from to increase to more than $300 million in 1997 from last year's about $200 million, it said.
Mesa said it expects to close the Greenhill transaction in April. It intends to fund the acquisition with bank financing committed by Chase Manhattan.
